title: Front doors for every house kind (cloud week 42, unit 9)
summary: Front doors for every house kind of Quay Street: from the passed 3.1 door (T1 cottage four-panel, F1 flat four-panel, its bell push fixed to one plain dark oblong), 10 door kinds (cottage T1 T2 T3, flat F1 to F7) fitted to the street's 12 household doors by house, 8 furniture slots with 28 variants (letter plates, handles, rim night latches, plugged keyholes, knockers, bells, numbers, a boot scraper), 15 paints and 3 conditions, a street order in which no two neighbours match, and a gate of 7 views a kind plus the street rows.
units: mm; leaf frame u across from the leaf's left edge seen from outside, v up from its bottom; frame frame x across the opening from the left reveal, z up from the threshold top (the 3.1 axes)

backdrop.rule: The 12 doors of the hill's rows (backdrop_rise_approach_e0 e1, w0 to w4, x0 to x4) are seen at 44 m and more: leaf kind and paint, nothing else. Door i takes kind BACKDROP_KINDS[i mod 6] and paint BACKDROP_PAINTS[(i + 2) mod 6], so that no two doors of a row, taken in their order, share a kind or a paint. No furniture, no step, no wear mask beyond the foot band.

mix_rule.text: A new house takes a kind its frame set allows (cottage frame T: T1 T2 T3; flat frame F: F1 to F7), a paint that is not its neighbours' on the same side nor the paint of a door within 4.6 m across the street, and furniture so that each neighbour differs in at least 2 of the slots letter plate, handle, latch, number. A modernised house (replacement windows) takes T3, F5 or F6 or keeps its old kind. Knockers, bells (except T1's oblong), black iron plates, bell pulls, frosted and wired glass and numerals in black metal are not placed on any house today.

build_door.py takes a kind (T1 T2 T3 F1 to F7) as well as the colour: the leaf, openings, mouldings and fittings come from target.json kinds and furniture; the frame set is T or F (every kind, F6 included, in its stops-in-front frame: the leaf opens inward, hinges inside).

New paints for --door-colour: deep_teal, cream, white_gloss, council_turquoise, olive, khaki, mustard, bright_blue, red, varnish (with the 3.1 six); --frame-colour takes white or white_grimy only (cream is dropped).

A condition parameter (kept, tired, neglected) sets the roughness and, for neglected, the eroded notch in the bottom rail (25 high, 60 to 200 wide, 3 deep, at the hinge side); the 2D wear layer's masks do the rest.
Behind every glazed kind (T2, T3, F4, F5 and every transom) the scene needs its own dark hall: the engine shows whatever is behind the glass (3.1 NOTES).
Check every kind with the 3.1 pass rule and the records of target.json checks; a push, a knocker or a plate the table does not place on a house is a fault.
covering_every_opening: Nothing may show through (check CV): in elevation the frame, the leaf, the glass and the transom cover the clear opening except the 10 mm foot gap and the leaf's 1.6 mm margins; at 60 degrees in plan the leaf laps 20.4 behind each stop and behind the transom's stop (the rows compute the lap from the frame's stop edges and the leaf's edges, and the setback of the leaf behind the stops from their depth), which closes the margin; every leaf lies behind its stops and opens inward; F7's boards are tongued and grooved with a tongue of at least 6 mm; the reveals' returns are the wall kit's (T: buff brick, 3.1 L1 to L5) and the shopfront's pilaster return (F: 24.4 a side); the 3.1 door review's dark hall is the render aid.
